prop: This design was built against the tetel repository at commit 57bd0e29a6c8bd3861f3982bebe3486f80e0453d with a clean working tree; every code citation below refers to that state.

TET-28's "workspace-rooted" requirement is NOT decidable from today's capture in the case that matters most. When look_grep finds matches, it records one extent entry per matched file, keyed on that file's resolved path, with label "<file> (grep: <pattern>)" — and the search root appears nowhere in what is captured; the code's own comment says the entries are keyed "not by the search root or the grep command line". A repo-wide grep and a single-file grep that matched the same file therefore capture byte-identical extents. Every genuine census of a symbol an implementer is told to modify falls in this positive-match case, because the symbol's definition site matches.

The zero-match case IS decidable today, and it shows the shape the fix should take: a no-match grep records one entry whose key is the resolved search root and whose Marker { root, state } is resolved from that same root, so "was this bounded negative repo-wide" reduces to comparing two tool-captured strings on one entry — key versus world_root. TET-5's per-observation markers and the unconditional -H made this comparison meaningful; they did not extend it to the positive-match case.

The census therefore needs a small capture extension before any refusal can exist: look_grep should record, for every search, one root-level search entry — key = the resolved search root, a label carrying the pattern and the match-file count, marker resolved from the search root — alongside the existing per-file match entries, making the match and no-match cases uniform. "Workspace-rooted" then has one decidable definition covering both cases: the search entry's key equals its own world_root, a byte comparison of two strings the same look_grep call captured from the same canonicalized directory. No author-typed input participates on either side.

A census check cannot be built on labels, and the record model already shows the right way to extend the schema. At mint time only key, label, world_root and world_state survive into an ExtentEntry — the observation's kind is dropped, and the grep pattern exists only inside a display label, where an author-chosen pattern containing " in " or "(grep: " would make parsing ambiguous. The census therefore needs the new root-level search entry to carry two structured fields into ExtentEntry — the observation kind and the search pattern — following the exact precedent world_root set: #[serde(default)], with the empty value read as "predates the field, not eligible" rather than guessed about. Legacy facts can then never satisfy a census requirement, whose remedy is precisely to re-run the grep under the new capture. The snapshot already ships facts.jsonl with full extent entries, so check reads these fields from files every snapshot already contains; and because no surface lets an author supply an extent by hand, both sides of the rooting comparison and the pattern are tool-captured by construction.

A mention-triggered refusal (candidate 2) is off-charter and already measured dead in this repository. The charter forbids heuristic refusals outright, and scope.rs records the measurement: string-matching symbol references was tried for the note-outside-extent check and rejected because it "would have flagged a legitimate quotation ... while missing both real overreaches" — naming a symbol is normal, concluding about it is the failure, "and those two are not distinguishable by string matching". A refusal wired to that detector would refuse honest memos, which is precisely what scope.rs's "refusing would make the honest case unwritable" disposition exists to prevent. This also means the README Direction entry for this feature — "requiring a workspace-rooted search behind a claim that names a symbol" — is phrased as the mention-triggered shape and should be corrected to the declared-target shape when this ships.

The decidable trigger is declaration (candidate 1): a modification target is a structured record the author creates — a symbol string plus a fact citation — and the refusal fires only on a declared target whose cited fact carries no qualifying census entry. This sits inside the machine partition's own stated principle, that machine failures are "objective contradictions between a document and the record it claims to rest on, decidable without a human": a target row is exactly a pointer at evidence, and "you did not point at your evidence" is the README's own example of a decidable question. The refusal's remedy is singular — run the workspace-rooted grep for that symbol, mint the fact, cite it (or withdraw the target) — so refusal rather than report is the right disposition for the declared-but-uncensused case, by the same discriminator under which scope.rs chose report: there, only a person can tell context from conclusion; here, nothing is left to tell.

Under-declaration — the memo recommends modifying a symbol it never declared — cannot be a refusal and must not be silently absorbed either. Deciding from prose that a sentence "tells an implementer to modify X" is a heuristic read of English, exactly the class the charter routes to the human-owed partition or nowhere; scope.rs's measured precedent shows the symbol-detector that trigger would need flags quotation and misses conclusion. The design therefore makes the omission visible instead of detected: (a) once a workspace declares any target, render emits a Modification targets section, and once any claim exists it emits the section even when empty — "Modification targets: none declared" — so a memo that recommends changes while declaring nothing shows a hole where the census should be, in front of every reader; and (b) check's standing non-coverage list, whose first entry is already "dependents that never declared themselves", gains a census-specific line ("a recommendation whose target was never declared") so the blind spot is printed rather than implicit.

Where the refusal lives, in both surfaces that can see it. (1) render --out refuses — the first content-conditional refusal in the render path, which today only warns (its pending-observations warning is deliberately "warned, never refused" because only the author can tell deliberate from forgotten; an uncensused declared target has no such honest reading). The refusal must live in one shared dispatch used by both CLI and MCP, because the render path has already grown a CLI/MCP drift once — workspace identity was minted by the CLI arm and not the MCP handler until the act moved into snapshot::write, the one shared place. (2) check re-verifies the rendered document against its snapshot as a machine failure, [uncensused-target], joining the partition's scope line; like notes_outside_extent and mint_windows it is computable only when a snapshot ships, so with no snapshot the target rows are reported human-owed as unverifiable, consistent with the existing deliberate choice that a missing snapshot is human-owed rather than a machine failure.

The rooting predicate — census entry's key byte-equals its own world_root — is satisfiable and fails closed. On this machine and repo the two spellings (fs-canonicalized search root; git rev-parse --show-toplevel) agree byte-for-byte, so an honestly rooted grep satisfies the predicate; and if the two tools ever disagree on spelling, the mismatch refuses an honest census loudly rather than accepting an unrooted one silently, because inequality can only ever deny rooting, never grant it. Two hardenings belong in the implementation: look_grep should itself compare the canonicalized search root against the marker's root at capture time and store the search entry's key in the marker's spelling when they name the same directory, so check stays a pure byte comparison; and the agreement should be pinned by a test, since one probe on one machine shows the common case, not an invariant.

The qualifying-census predicate, fully: a declared target (symbol S, citing fact F) is censused iff F's captured extent contains a search entry whose kind field says it is a whole-search record, whose pattern field byte-equals S, whose key byte-equals its own world_root, and whose world_root is git-backed (neither the no-git sentinel nor the empty predates-the-field value). Byte-equality of pattern to symbol is the only sound decidable comparison available: grep is invoked with the pattern verbatim (-e <pattern>), so a looser rule like "pattern contains the symbol" would accept a grep whose pattern merely embeds S in a longer string and therefore matches a strict subset of S's textual occurrences, while anything semantically wider would require deciding containment between regular expressions. Symbols that are not literal strings in the system grep's dialect are a stated limit of the census, not a case the check adjudicates.

The census's blind spots are boundable from what the capture actually does, and belong in check's printed non-coverage: (a) a textual grep cannot see dynamic dispatch, re-exports and aliased imports, or macro-generated and string-assembled identifiers; (b) the traversal is the system grep's — tetel deliberately shells out to it rather than reimplementing a dialect — so platform rules about symlinked directories and the -I binary skip bound what a "repo-wide" search physically visited; (c) rooting says where the search started, not which tree it should have been: whether the censused root is the tree the memo designs against stays with the reader, alongside the existing per-root tree-state report; (d) whether anyone read the census is the insincere-examination ceiling — capture makes the extent honest, not the interpretation; and (e) under-declared targets, by construction. The report mechanism for printing exactly this kind of standing limit already exists as the NON_COVERAGE list.

The feature's implementation surface is small and depends on nothing beyond what this memo's facts describe: one additional recorded entry in look_grep, two serde-defaulted structured fields on the extent entry (following world_root's own compatibility precedent), one new append-only record type with an authoring verb, one rendered section beside the existing ledger and Facts tables, one refusal in a shared render dispatch, and one machine check with its human-owed and non-coverage lines. In particular it requires no TET-27 mechanism — no code-to-graph links, no commit references, no dependency propagation — so shipping it first imposes no design debt on that exploration.

Where the refusal lives: at declaration, then re-verified at check. The `target` verb refuses to create a target whose cited fact carries no qualifying census entry — the same authoring-time shape as fact refusing on an empty pending buffer ("a fact needs a preceding look/run"; a target needs a preceding rooted census). Because a fact's extent is immutable once minted and a target is immutable once declared, this makes "every declared target is censused" a workspace invariant, and no render-path refusal is needed for workspace-authored documents; render's job is only to emit the targets section. check independently re-verifies the rendered document against its snapshot and reports [uncensused-target] as a machine failure in the partition's scope line, which is what catches a hand-authored or tampered document that never passed through the refusing verb. Like notes_outside_extent and mint_windows, that check runs only when a snapshot ships; without one, target rows are reported human-owed as unverifiable, consistent with the standing choice that a missing snapshot is human-owed rather than a machine failure. The verb must be one dispatch shared by CLI and MCP, the pattern look and fact already use, because this codebase has recorded a CLI/MCP drift on exactly such a duplicated act.
why: F3 shows the stronger precedent this claim under-used: fact's own empty-buffer refusal establishes authoring-time refusal as the house shape, and applying the census predicate at target creation makes "declared implies censused" a workspace invariant — facts' extents and targets are both immutable — so the render-path refusal in the earlier wording becomes dead code guarding an unreachable state. The check-side verification and the missing-snapshot disposition are unchanged.

prop: The ticket's trigger as written is undecidable in tetel's own record model, verified against the record types: a claim is only { id, proposition, cited fact ids, withdrawn }, a prose block only { heading, level, text, cited claim ids }, and nothing on either surface types a record as a recommendation or an instruction — prose creation is deliberately ungated because "prose is where the author talks, not where they're audited". So "a memo whose recommendation names a target" denotes no set of records any check can enumerate; any implementation of it would have to read English. The claim verb also supplies the refusal precedent the target verb extends: claim already refuses without --cites and on unknown fact ids, so "a structured record must cite a real record of the right shape" is the house's established authoring-refusal pattern.

This design was built against the tetel repository at commit 57bd0e29a6c8bd3861f3982bebe3486f80e0453d; at the start of authoring, before this memo and its snapshot were themselves written into docs/design/, git status --porcelain printed nothing. Every code citation below refers to that commit; the memo's own output files are the one addition to the tree this workspace makes.
why: Grounding pass k1 qualified this: "clean working tree" holds only up to the memo's own untracked artifacts, which exist once the memo is rendered into the repo. F1's observation was taken before they existed; the claim now states its own timing instead of asserting a tree state the act of rendering necessarily ends.

prop: A census enumerates call sites, not the modes those sites select, and this is a distinct printed limit rather than the insincere-examination ceiling restated. Distinct because the two limits bound different things: the ceiling bounds interpretation — capture makes the extent honest, not the reading of it — while the mode limit bounds the artifact itself. What look_grep captures per matched file is the matching lines only; an argument that selects materially different behaviour (a None versus a Some, a flag, a mode enum) is sometimes visible on a match line, never enumerated, and absent entirely when the value arrives through a variable, a default, or another line of a multi-line call. So even a sincerely read census does not, in general, contain which mechanism each caller engages — the reader must leave the census and read the callee and each call's context, which is why collapsing this into "whether anyone read the census" would misstate the remedy. It does not change the design: surfacing argument values at census time would require parsing call expressions, which is per-language knowledge — exactly the coupling the project's language-agnostic-by-construction doctrine exists to exclude — and it would not change the trigger either, since a value-surfacing census would still need the same declared-target trigger. It costs one more line in the census's non-coverage: the census gets an implementer to the door of every textual call site; it does not say what happens inside any of them.
